title: Reduction to finitely many degrees
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme, $\ell$ a prime, $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $E\subseteq\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, understood as the condensed coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] or [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], respectively, and put $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], with $d_C\geq0$ as in [sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext], and let $m\in\mathbf Z$.
Here $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ consists of the $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves that are filtered colimits of constructible sheaves, and $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ is the full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$ whose cohomology sheaves all belong to $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $K\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$. Use canonical truncations and cohomological shifts, with $H^q(K[s])=H^{q+s}(K)$ [def-kun-truncations]. All Hom groups are taken in $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda_X)$, with $C$ placed in degree zero. The truncation maps induce a natural isomorphism
$$
\Hom(C,K[m])\cong\Hom\bigl(C,(\tau_{\geq m-d_C}\tau_{\leq m}K)[m]\bigr).
$$
Thus maps out of $C$ see only the cohomology degrees $m-d_C,\ldots,m$ of $K$, even when $K$ is unbounded.

proof.text:
Work directly at the given degree $m$. Put $d=d_C$, $A=\tau_{\leq m}K$, $U=\tau_{\geq m+1}K$, $V=\tau_{\leq m-d-1}A$, and $B=\tau_{\geq m-d}A$. The canonical truncation triangles are
$$A\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow U\longrightarrow A[1],\qquad V\longrightarrow A\longrightarrow B\longrightarrow V[1].$$
These exist without any boundedness hypothesis by [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] (Stacks Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle). By the good-truncation formulas of [def-kun-truncations], each cohomology sheaf of $A$ and $V$ is either a cohomology sheaf of $K$ or zero. The zero sheaf is constructible (take the zero finite local model on every stratum), hence ind-constructible via the constant filtered diagram. Thus $A,V\in\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ by its defining condition. Also $V[m]$ and $V[m+1]$ are in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$, since a shift merely reindexes the cohomology sheaves.

source.place: paragraph 1, upper and lower truncation triangles; retain the given m rather than shift the notation

proof.text:
The upper tail satisfies $U[m]\in D^{\geq1}$ and $U[m-1]\in D^{\geq2}\subset D^{\geq1}$, whereas the sheaf $C$ in degree zero lies in $D^{\leq0}$. The standard t-structure and its orthogonality axiom give $\Hom(C,U[m])=\Hom(C,U[m-1])=0$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], [def-weil-t-structure]. Shift the first triangle of step 1 by $m$ and apply $\Hom(C,-)$. Exactness for a distinguished triangle and its rotations [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] (Stacks Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological) gives
$$0\longrightarrow\Hom(C,A[m])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,K[m])\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular the map $a_K:\Hom(C,A[m])\to\Hom(C,K[m])$ induced by upper truncation is an isomorphism.

source.place: paragraph 1, vanishing of the upper tail and upper truncation isomorphism

proof.text:
We have $H^q(V[m])=0$ for $q>-d-1$, and $H^q(V[m+1])=0$ for $q>-d-2$. Both satisfy the bound $q>-d_C-1$ in [det-finite-window-unbounded], and their membership in $\Dic(X,\Lambda)$ was checked in step 1. That existing node, which has no lower boundedness hypothesis, therefore gives $\Hom(C,V[m])=\Hom(C,V[m+1])=0$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to the second triangle of step 1 shifted by $m$, and to its rotations, yields
$$0\longrightarrow\Hom(C,A[m])\longrightarrow\Hom(C,B[m])\longrightarrow0.$$
Consequently the map $b_K:\Hom(C,A[m])\to\Hom(C,B[m])$ induced by lower truncation is an isomorphism. The lower-tail node carries precisely the bounded-devissage and left-completeness/Milnor arguments in paragraphs 2--4 of the source; no compactness assertion is used here.

source.place: paragraph 1, lower truncation exact sequence, using the lower-tail conclusion of paragraphs 2--4

proof.text: The required map is $b_K\circ a_K^{-1}$. Since $B=\tau_{\geq m-d_C}\tau_{\leq m}K$, its source and target are exactly the displayed Hom groups. For a morphism $f:K\to\widetilde K$, let $F$, $F_A$, and $F_B$ be its induced maps on $\Hom(C,K[m])$, $\Hom(C,A[m])$, and $\Hom(C,B[m])$, respectively. Functoriality of the canonical truncations [def-kun-truncations] gives $F a_K=a_{\widetilde K}F_A$ and $F_B b_K=b_{\widetilde K}F_A$. Therefore $F_Aa_K^{-1}=a_{\widetilde K}^{-1}F$ and $F_Bb_Ka_K^{-1}=b_{\widetilde K}F_Aa_K^{-1}=b_{\widetilde K}a_{\widetilde K}^{-1}F$. This proves naturality in $K$ for fixed $C,d_C,m$. The argument includes $C=0$, $K=0$, $d_C=0$ and arbitrary positive or negative $m$.

lean.note: Two statements cover the finite-extension and algebraic-closure coefficients. The subtype indexing the additive equivalences is exactly the object class Dic in the ambient ordinary unbounded derived category. The first equation characterizes the canonical truncation zigzag, and the second asserts naturality in every ambient morphism of Dic objects. The uniform Ext bound is an explicit hypothesis, as in the already stated lower-tail lemma; no geometric restrictions on X or boundedness of K are imposed. FiniteWindowAssertions transparently packages the equivalence family and its two equations over an arbitrary abelian category, avoiding repetition of the large coefficient-category expression during compiled-module export. It contains only the exact conclusion and no chosen data.
